New Card Modes

Five modes, two or three options each, drawn with the mod's own card and tab code at the band's real size. Every card shows the same session: 62% context, 5-hour 34%, week 58%, Fable 41%, $21.37, 61 turns.

VU

CB meter ↗Tuner dial ↗

Twin meters

Recommended
  • The sketch the owner picked, made real: two backlit faces you read from across the room.
  • Peak lamp and red zone say "near the limit" without words.
  • Two meters take 300 px before any number shows.
  • Week and Fable only as small edgewise meters on the plate.

The numbers go first, then the 5-hour meter moves onto the plate as a third edgewise row. The context meter stays.

Sport lights the peak lamps and turns the percent red. Eco and Normal look alike: needles low, lamps dark.

Night dial

  • Closest to the pin: cyan print on black, a warm bezel glow, a thin copper needle.
  • Three scales in one window: context, 5-hour and week, each a row of lit segments with its last fifth in green.
  • Segments read less precisely than a needle; the figures carry the detail.
  • Cooler colours than the amber sketch.

The numbers go first. The dial keeps its 236 px; the plate keeps Fable.

Sport fills the green end segments on every scale. Eco leaves most segments as ghosts.

Meter bridge

  • Every limit gets a real needle: context, 5-hour, week and Fable side by side, like a tape machine's meter bridge.
  • Four faces at 100 px are busy and the scale numbers get small.
  • Numbers move to the plate or drop.

Meters leave from the right (Fable, then week) and reappear on the plate as edgewise rows.

Sport: two peak lamps lit, percents red.

Nixie

Nixie digits ↗

Tubes and bars

Recommended
  • Context in two big wire-digit tubes with every other cathode visible behind.
  • Limits on IN-13 bar tubes: a glowing column, a cold mark at pace.
  • Session numbers stay readable as glowing text.
  • Only context is in tubes; the rest is styled text.

The numbers go first, from the right. Tubes and the bar plate stay.

Sport: the context tubes and over-pace bars turn red and the neon lamp by the % lights.

Tube clock

  • All in tubes, like a nixie clock: context, cost with its decimal dot, time with neon colon lamps, turns.
  • Each limit is a pair of small tubes with a neon lamp that lights when it runs ahead.
  • No bars, so pace is only the lamp.
  • Tokens, cache and written are left out.

Groups leave from the right: turns, then time, then cost. Context stays.

Sport: tubes over pace glow red and their lamps light.

Cockpit

Aspen PFD ↗PFD concept ↗

Flight tapes

Recommended
  • The PFD language: a rolling context tape with a boxed value and a drum for the last digit.
  • Limit tapes with a green fill, amber and red range stripe, magenta pace bug.
  • A master caution box on the plate.
  • Dense. Many small parts at 93 px.

The data block goes first, then the limit tapes shorten to 120 px. The context tape stays.

Sport: fills turn amber or red and the plate shows LIMIT (or CTX in red at 90%).

Engine dials

  • EICAS engine dials: three round gauges with filled arcs and boxed values.
  • Reads at a glance, like the engine page.
  • Dials are small (25 px radius).
  • Less like the Aspen pin, more like an airliner.

The data block goes first; the three dials stay.

Sport: values amber or red, caution box on the plate.

LCD

Charger ↗Synth LCD ↗

Whole screen

Recommended
  • The whole card is a backlit character LCD; every cell shows its unlit dots.
  • Bars are dot grids with a stepped head and the percent riding on it, as in the charger pin.
  • The backlight turns amber in Sport: the strongest state change of the five.
  • The only bright card in the set besides Panel.
  • The rail needs the black bezel: grey glyphs on lime would not read.

Reset times go first, then the bars shorten to 20 cells. The numbers stay on the plate.

Sport turns the backlight amber. Eco and Normal are green.

Screen in a device

  • A pale, cool LCD set into a dark device, like the synth pin.
  • Dark card overall; only the window is bright.
  • Session numbers printed on the device face in white.
  • The screen is smaller; bars have 24 cells.

The printed numbers go first, then the window narrows.

Sport turns the window amber.

Panel

Synth UI ↗Control kit ↗

Knobs and screen

Recommended
  • The sketch made real: one coloured knob per meter, a black OLED, keys lit at the rim.
  • The only light card in the set.
  • Tabs stay dark: the app writes the update label and rail glyphs in its own colours, which are light in the dark theme.
  • Bright against the black app.

The OLED shrinks to the context figure, then goes. Knobs stay; cost, time and turns move onto the plate.

Sport turns over-pace knob rings and the mode key's rim red.

Wide screen

  • Aluminium frame round a wide OLED with OP-1 style colour bars.
  • More numbers fit; bars are inset grooves with pace dots.
  • Fewer physical knobs, so less of the TE feel.

The OLED's number column goes first, then the bars shorten.

Sport turns over-pace bars red.

Space grey

  • Same layout as Knobs and screen in space grey: fits the black app, tabs blend in.
  • Loses what makes Panel different from the other nine: being light.

As Knobs and screen.

As Knobs and screen.

Picking among ten

Today the mode button steps through five. With ten, a full round is nine presses.

Picker on the card

Recommended
◐ Glass◒ Cluster◓ Tuner▦ Board◑ Classic◠ VU◍ Nixie△ Cockpit▤ LCD◎ Panel
  • Press the mode button: the card turns into a row of the ten names. Press one to switch; the card comes back.
  • Any mode in one press, and the names teach what exists.
  • Ten buttons at 8 px per cell need about 700 px; a narrow pane wraps them onto two lines.

Keep one cycle of ten

  • Up to nine presses to reach a mode.

Found while drawing

  • The rail's three glyphs and the update tab's label are the app's own text, grey and white in the dark theme. A light card needs dark keys under the rail and a dark update tab, or they disappear. Panel and LCD do this.
  • The room above the card (where the tabs stand) is painted #0a0a0a in tab.ts, whatever the theme. On the light theme every mode shows a black strip there. The light-page pictures above repaint it; the build would take the page colour from the theme.
  • The project tab's name and branch are drawn white in tab.ts. Every new mode keeps a dark tab, Panel included.
